business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Strongly backward integrated: in-house production of key inputs including aluminium wire rods, aluminium alloy rods and XLPE/PVC compound, plus an in-house compounding facility for insulation, sheathing and semi-conductive materials used across power cables and conductors. Company manufactures its own wooden drums and packing materials and recycles/reprocesses scrap PVC/XLPE. Installed capacity for manufactured products increased by approximately 37.82% between Fiscal 2024 and Fiscal 2026. Internal purchase of company-manufactured products used in EPC projects rose from Rs 2,596.41 million (Fiscal 2024) to Rs 3,052.71 million (Fiscal 2025) to Rs 3,543.86 million (Fiscal 2026). Forward integrated into EPC segment (entered 2015), providing cross-feeding of conductors and cables for its own EPC projects; apart from certain civil works, all EPC work is executed in-house with no third-party subcontracting.

overview.business_model: Manufactures power cables, conductors, aluminium wire rods and HT covered conductors across three West Bengal units (Dhulagarh Units I and II, and Kharagpur Unit III) with a combined installed capacity of 85,448 MT, and executes engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contracts for rural electrification, power distribution infrastructure and substations. Key customers are state and central government organisations, state electricity boards and public and private power utilities, largely won through tenders. The manufacturing segment also supplies the in-house EPC segment on an arm's-length basis (inter-segment revenue eliminated on consolidation).

genesis.founding_story: Originally incorporated as 'Laser Cables Private Limited' at Kolkata, West Bengal as a private limited company under the Companies Act, 1956. Over an operating history spanning more than three decades it built a power cables and conductors manufacturing business, and in 2015 expanded into the EPC segment in the power distribution sector as part of a forward-integration strategy.

Adverse developments in manufacturing performance, changes in consumer preferences, technological advancements, increased competition, quality lapses, product recalls, economic downturns, supply chain disruptions, or reduction in government budgetary allocation for transmission and distribution networks could materially adversely affect business, cash flows, results of operations and financial position.
internal_operational.evidence: Fiscal 2026: Manufacturing ₹16,910.39 million (72.70%), EPC ₹6,350.65 million (27.30%). Fiscal 2025: Manufacturing ₹18,570.48 million (72.25%), EPC ₹7,133.49 million (27.75%). Fiscal 2024: Manufacturing ₹15,278.28 million (87.43%), EPC ₹2,197.50 million (12.57%).
internal_operational.title: Dependence on manufacturing segment – power cables and conductors

internal_operational.detail: Operations depend on prices and availability of aluminium, steel, copper, XLPE and PVC compound. Cost of materials consumed was 63.35%, 61.04% and 62.99% of total expenses in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. Fluctuations in commodity prices, supply chain disruptions, inadequate transportation, inclement weather, labour unrest, regulatory changes, tariffs and currency exchange rates could affect estimated costs, expenditures and timelines. Price escalation mechanisms exist but no assurance of future ability to pass on cost increases. Typically maintain 20-31 days of inventory for primary raw materials; occasional shortages have occurred.
internal_operational.evidence: Fiscal 2026: Cost of materials consumed ₹13,855.40 million (63.35% of total expenses ₹21,870.33 million); 96.64% sourced from India. Fiscal 2025: ₹14,981.47 million (61.04% of ₹24,543.88 million); 96.31% from India. Fiscal 2024: ₹10,769.64 million (62.99% of ₹17,096.04 million); 94.29% from India.

strategy_growth.detail: The power infrastructure sector is highly competitive with competition from domestic and international manufacturers and EPC players. EPC segment primarily procures projects on competitive bidding, sometimes requiring aggressive pricing. The Company may not be able to aggressively price services in the future. Key competitors in cables and conductors industry include Apar Industries Limited, Dynamic Cables Limited, KEI Industries Limited, and Polycab India Limited. Competitors might develop new technologies that cause existing offerings to become less competitive.

strategy_growth.detail: The Company is actively seeking to diversify its EPC portfolio by expanding into water distribution lines, solar, and battery energy storage systems sectors. This introduces operational, financial, and market risks. Existing expertise is primarily in the power sector; water distribution sectors have distinct technical, regulatory, and market dynamics. Complexity could result in delays, cost overruns, and technical difficulties. Changes in government policies or regulations could make projects financially unfeasible. Competition in these markets may be intense.

concerns_observed: High customer concentration: Top 10 customers contributed 72.14% (FY26), 68.87% (FY25), 53.37% (FY24) of revenue; single largest customer 24.82% in FY26.
High supplier concentration: Top 10 suppliers accounted for 67.73% (FY26), 60.49% (FY25), 61.58% (FY24) of purchases; Vedanta Limited alone 24.06% in FY26.
Declining capacity utilization: Total utilization dropped from 85.79% (FY24) to 76.23% (FY25) to 61.59% (FY26) while installed capacity increased ~37.82%.
Working capital intensive with high trade receivables: 59.11% of revenue (FY26), 43.57% (FY25), 45.06% (FY24); government contracts entail long credit periods.
Significant indebtedness: Total borrowings ₹8,282.34 million (FY26), ₹5,029.49 million (FY25), ₹3,937.49 million (FY24); unsecured loans ₹4,613.59 million (FY26) repayable on demand.
Financing agreements contain restrictive covenants limiting capital structure changes, dividends, new borrowings, and requiring lender consent for key corporate actions.
EPC segment dependent on competitive bidding with low bid-to-win ratios: 16.42% (FY26), 23.76% (FY25), 14.70% (FY24); fixed-price contracts expose to cost overruns.
All three manufacturing units concentrated in West Bengal, exposing to regional risks (natural disasters, regulatory changes, labour unrest).
High attrition rates: 18.25% (FY26), 26.39% (FY25), 19.93% (FY24); no succession plan adopted.
Heavy reliance on third-party contract labour: 2,170 (FY26), 2,147 (FY25) on third-party payroll in manufacturing.
Audit reports for FY24–FY26 contain emphasis of matter on outstanding title deeds, working capital statement differences, related-party loans/guarantees, and disputed statutory dues.
Promoter average cost of acquisition extremely low (₹0.01 to Nil per share) versus Offer Price; bonus issue 8:1 within 18 months of DRHP.
Certain historical corporate records for allotments not traceable, posing risk of future legal/regulatory actions.
Multiple complex corporate restructurings (Scheme of Amalgamation 2011, Composite Scheme of Arrangement 2022) with numerous related-party transactions.
No long-term supply contracts; raw material price volatility risk (cost of materials consumed 63.35% of total expenses in FY26).
Late delivery deductions by customers: ₹3.48 million (FY26), ₹7.88 million (FY25), ₹17.41 million (FY24).

verdict.our_read: An improving cable + EPC maker (RoNW 8->21%, order book Rs 3,243 cr) weighed down by red flags: audit emphasis-of-matter three years running, promoter cost ~Rs 0.01/share, and utilisation falling to 62% even as capacity was expanded 38%.

parameter_scores.basis: Integrated manufacturing + EPC model with backward integration provides cost advantages, but heavy dependence on power infrastructure sector, government budgetary allocations, and top 10 customers (72.14% of revenue in FY26) creates vulnerability. Manufacturing segment alone contributed 72.70% of revenue in FY26. Capacity utilization declining to 61.59% despite capacity expansion signals demand-supply mismatch risk.

Total borrowings ₹8,282.34 million (FY26) with finance costs ₹1,331.06 million; interest coverage ratio 2.21x (FY26). Unsecured loans ₹4,613.59 million repayable on demand. Restrictive covenants in financing agreements. Trade receivables ₹13,749.57 million (59.11% of revenue). Net working capital ₹10,206.62 million. EBITDA margins improving but absolute debt levels rising significantly (FY24: ₹3,937.49 million → FY26: ₹8,282.34 million).

Promoters hold majority post-Offer; average acquisition cost ₹0.01 to Nil. Multiple complex restructurings and untraceable historical allotment records. Audit reports contain emphasis of matter for three consecutive years. Board has 3 independent directors out of 6. Promoter Deepak Goel has no formal education; Promoter Rakhi Goel has no professional experience beyond being a promoter. High number of other directorships for executive directors (Devesh Goel: 13, Akshat Goel: 12). No succession plan. KMP attrition: Whole-time Director Navin Kumar Saffar resigned June 30, 2025.

Installed capacity 85,448 MT but utilization only 61.59% (FY26). EPC bid-to-win ratio low (16.42% FY26). High dependence on contract labour (2,170 on third-party payroll FY26). Attrition 18.25% (FY26). All plants in West Bengal (concentration risk). Backward integration and TS Conductor partnership support scalability, but under-utilization and regional concentration limit operational flexibility.

Positioned as one of the leading players in East India for power cables and conductors. Strategic partnership with TS Conductor Corp for advanced conductors provides differentiation. Marquee government customer base (65.16% of revenue FY26). However, intense competition from larger national players (Polycab, KEI, Apar Industries) with significantly higher revenues and profitability. No disclosed market share percentage. Export revenue declining (4.17% FY24 → 2.19% FY26).

Multiple internal operational risks identified: customer concentration, supplier concentration, raw material price volatility, EPC execution risks, labour dependency, IT system vulnerability, insufficient insurance (18.04% assets uninsured FY26). Audit emphasis of matter for three years. Contingent liabilities ₹267.83 million (FY26). Historical corporate records not traceable. No past non-compliance table provided in extracted sections. Late delivery deductions indicate execution challenges.

red_flags: Audit reports for three consecutive fiscals (FY24, FY25, FY26) contain emphasis of matter on outstanding title deeds, working capital statement differences to banks, related-party loans/guarantees, and disputed statutory dues — indicating persistent governance/accounting concerns.

Promoter average cost of acquisition is ₹0.01 to Nil per share, while Offer Price is to be determined through book-building; combined with 8:1 bonus issue within 18 months of DRHP, raises significant dilution and promoter exit concerns.
Certain historical corporate records for allotments are not traceable, posing risk of future legal or regulatory actions on share capital validity.
Total borrowings surged from ₹3,937.49 million (FY24) to ₹8,282.34 million (FY26) with ₹4,613.59 million in unsecured loans repayable on demand — liquidity and refinancing risk is material.
Capacity utilization dropped to 61.59% in FY26 while installed capacity was expanded by ~37.82% over two years — suggests either aggressive capacity build-up ahead of demand or demand contraction.
Top 10 customers contributed 72.14% of revenue in FY26 with single largest customer at 24.82%; combined with government entity payment delays and state DISCOM indebtedness, receivables risk is acute.
No succession plan despite high dependence on Key Managerial Personnel and 18.25% attrition rate; Whole-time Director resigned in June 2025.
strengths_observed: Robust order book of ₹32,434.00 million as of March 31, 2026, providing long-term revenue visibility.
Strong backward integration (in-house aluminium rods, alloy rods, PVC compounds, packaging) reducing supplier dependency and enhancing cost control.
Strategic partnership with TS Conductor Corp for advanced high-capacity conductors (AECC/TS Conductors).
Established track record with marquee government and private customers; government revenue share increased to 65.16% in Fiscal 2026.
Leading manufacturing capacity for power cables and conductors in East India with integrated EPC capabilities.
Diversified product portfolio covering LV/MV power cables, conductors (ACSR, AAC, AAAC, advanced TS conductors), and specialty products.
Experienced promoters (Deepak Goel: >37 years in cable/power industry) and management team.
Certifications: ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, BIS, NABL-accredited lab, RDSO-accredited supplier.

sk.overview: Powerica operates across two industries: (1) India's standby power / diesel-generator (DG set) market, where DG sets, UPS, inverters and battery storage provide backup power during outages/voltage fluctuations across commercial, manufacturing, IT/data-centre, telecom and infrastructure sectors (F&S Report); and (2) India's wind power sector within the broader renewable energy industry, where wind plays a pivotal role in the country's energy transition (CRISIL Report).
